name: Marsilea

project_scope.source: Live Master Plant Pool + existing Marsileaceae family.json, 2026-10-12
project_scope.selection_note: Genus comparison only. No species installation, taxonomic re-adjudication, or target-zone range certification.

shared_genus_recognition.look_here_first: Find a four-part, clover-like frond, then TRACE ITS PETIOLE DOWN to the creeping rhizome. Search for hard, bean-like SPOROCARPS at or near the petiole base; on mature sporocarps compare the stalk, orientation, and distal tooth.
shared_traits: Rooted aquatic/amphibious ferns spreading by creeping rhizomes; roots emerge at nodes.
Frond typically has four wedge- or fan-shaped pinnae at the end of a long petiole, but frond size changes with water depth and conditions.
No flowers, petals, fruits, or seeds. The hard sporocarp contains sori bearing microspores and megaspores.
Species separation requires mature attached sporocarps whenever possible; sterile leaves often do not support a secure identification.
shared_genus_recognition.family_door: Compare with Trifolium repens (Fabaceae; three leaflets, flower heads and seed pods), Oxalis spp. (Oxalidaceae; usually three heart-shaped leaflets and flowers), and Azolla caroliniana (Salviniaceae; tiny floating fern with overlapping scale-like leaves rather than long-stalked four-pinna fronds).

look_here_first_sequence: 1. Confirm Marsilea by a four-pinna frond, creeping rhizome, and hard sporocarps near the petiole base; do not mistake sporocarps for seeds.
2. On several mature sporocarps, TRACE THE STALK: branched stalks strongly support M. macropoda; consistently unbranched stalks require checking the tooth and orientation for M. vestita.

3. Examine the sporocarp IN SIDE VIEW at 10–20×: strongly ascending with a missing/weak distal tooth favors M. macropoda; transverse to slightly nodding with a sharp, sometimes hooked distal tooth favors M. vestita.
4. Check the leaflet underside and margin: conspicuous white hairs projecting beyond the margin favor M. macropoda, but hairiness alone is not decisive.
5. If sterile, juvenile, damaged, or intermediate, record Marsilea sp. and photograph attached mature sporocarps rather than forcing a species.

species_comparison_matrix.Marsilea macropoda: Erect stalk frequently BRANCHED; unbranched stalks also occur.
species_comparison_matrix.caution: An unbranched M. macropoda stalk can mimic M. vestita. Examine several stalks.
species_comparison_matrix.photo_role: Matched close-up from petiole attachment through complete stalk and all sporocarps.

species_comparison_matrix.Marsilea vestita: Sporocarps approximately PERPENDICULAR to stalk or slightly NODDING.
species_comparison_matrix.caution: Keep stalk and sporocarp in same side-view frame; specimen handling can change apparent angle.
species_comparison_matrix.photo_role: Paired lateral macros showing stalk-to-sporocarp angle.

species_comparison_matrix.Marsilea macropoda: Absent or only a slightly raised area.
species_comparison_matrix.Marsilea vestita: Distinct, acute distal tooth about 0.4–1.2 mm, often hooked.
species_comparison_matrix.caution: Inspect mature, intact sporocarps with magnification; do not confuse the proximal blunt tooth with the distal one.
species_comparison_matrix.photo_role: Matched 10–20× side macros with arrows separately labeling distal tooth, proximal tooth and raphe.

species_comparison_matrix.caution: Strong numerical overlap; proximal tooth does NOT separate the pair on its own.
species_comparison_matrix.photo_role: Same tooth macros with millimeter calibration.

species_comparison_matrix.caution: Dimensions overlap substantially; measure several mature sporocarps.
species_comparison_matrix.photo_role: Paired intact sporocarps beside a millimeter ruler, side-on.

species_comparison_matrix.Marsilea vestita: At base, occasionally as much as 3 mm above it.
species_comparison_matrix.caution: Overlap around 2–3 mm. Preserve the entire base in the image.
species_comparison_matrix.photo_role: Base macro with petiole origin, rhizome and stalk attachment all visible.

species_comparison_matrix.caution: Ranges overlap; water depth and leaf development change size.
species_comparison_matrix.photo_role: Mature fronds from same habitat state, top view with scale.

species_comparison_matrix.Marsilea macropoda: Conspicuously WHITE-HAIRY beneath; hairs often project beyond leaflet margin.
species_comparison_matrix.Marsilea vestita: Sparsely hairy to nearly hairless with age; leaflets may be hairy or glabrescent.
species_comparison_matrix.caution: Hair abrasion and leaf age matter; do not key on color or hair alone.
species_comparison_matrix.photo_role: Matched underside and edge macro with light revealing projecting hairs.

species_comparison_matrix.caution: Broad overlap and plastic response to depth; never use as primary ID.
species_comparison_matrix.photo_role: Whole rooted plants with petiole scale and water-depth context.

species_comparison_matrix.caution: Broad overlap and requires dissection; teaching anatomy only.
species_comparison_matrix.photo_role: Dissected sporocarp with sori labeled; optional specialist view.

overlap_cautions: Do not identify sterile four-pinna leaves to species from leaflet size or hairiness alone.
M. macropoda can have unbranched sporocarp stalks; combine orientation, distal tooth and foliage.
Sporocarp length, stalk attachment, petiole length and sori counts overlap.

The existing family lesson flags putative M. macropoda × M. vestita intermediates reported from Blanco County (within the project target zone). Do not force an intermediate to either species; request review and voucher-quality images.
No native-range decision is implied by inclusion in this source-pool lesson.

local_source_pool_lookalikes.why_confused: Clover-like leaves on low wet-ground vegetation.
local_source_pool_lookalikes.look_here_first: Three leaflets, rounded flower heads and legume fruits; Marsilea has four pinnae and fern sporocarps, no flowers.

local_source_pool_lookalikes.why_confused: Low three-leaflet plants mistaken for water clover.
local_source_pool_lookalikes.look_here_first: Three often notched/heart-shaped leaflets, five-petaled flowers and capsules; Marsilea has four pinnae and sporocarps.

local_source_pool_lookalikes.why_confused: Small wetland fern in the same order Salviniales.
local_source_pool_lookalikes.look_here_first: Tiny free-floating branching mat with overlapping scale leaves, not rooted long-petioled four-pinna fronds.

local_source_pool_lookalikes.taxon: Other Marsilea spp. in broader regional floras
local_source_pool_lookalikes.why_confused: Non-pool species and historical names can occur in keys.
local_source_pool_lookalikes.look_here_first: Use full regional key if mature sporocarps disagree with either species; do not add an extra project taxon without approved source-pool/identity work.

diagnostic_photo_checklist.capture: Mature stalks still attached to petiole base; label branch points and each sporocarp; 10× view.
Keep entire stalk and sporocarp in focus; label angle; add scale.

diagnostic_photo_checklist.character: weak/absent versus acute hooked distal tooth
diagnostic_photo_checklist.capture: 10–20× or higher with millimeter scale; arrows to distal tooth, proximal tooth and raphe; inspect several intact mature sporocarps.
Show rhizome, petiole origin and stalk origin in one frame, with millimeter scale.

diagnostic_photo_checklist.character: white projecting hairs versus sparse/glabrescent surface
diagnostic_photo_checklist.capture: Same magnification and side-lighting; label abaxial surface and margin.

diagnostic_photo_checklist.character: four pinnae, leaflet/petiole sizes, water depth
diagnostic_photo_checklist.capture: Fronds with 5 cm scale; show rhizome, mature frond, and water-depth context.
If a verified specimen is available, show at least two conflicting characters; mark intermediate/undetermined, not a species ID.
Clearly label sporocarp, sori, megaspores, microspores; diagram is teaching supplement, not species diagnosis.

existing_media_reuse.note: Existing family visual lesson supplies validated teaching targets but no exact image IDs were confirmed during this run. Do not invent Joey/user photo references; Diagnostic Photo Polish should check routing index and provenance before attaching any.

handoffs.request: Acquire exact-species provenance-tracked macros for branching, sporocarp angle, distal tooth, and petiole-base attachment first; family module has anatomical teaching requirements.

handoffs.target: Marsilea macropoda × M. vestita putative Blanco County intermediates
handoffs.request: Confirm the family-module report of putative hybrid/intermediate populations in Blanco County against FNA/vouchers, and specify a stop-at-genus decision rule for discordant specimens. Do not change settled species concepts.
Both names occur in approved source pool and are absent from current canonical manifest. Species installation and taxonomic identity checks belong to installer, not this genus lesson.
